name: transfer333-owner-authorized-certification
purpose: Make a policy-bound owner signature plus executable account-state preflight the only path into the Byzantine-safe authority certification rail, and settle certificates without splitting authority balance from sequence state.

fit_evidence: All authority transports require the same owner-authentication and account-slot admission semantics.
The immutable owner roster and network identity are verifier-owned trust roots shared by authorities, collectors, and ledger replicas.
alternatives_considered: Trust a caller-supplied public key, rejected because it does not bind the string AccountId to its owner.
Immediately replace AccountId with a self-certifying NodeId, deferred because it would combine the security fix with a repository-wide identity migration.

boundary.owns: Owner-proof validation, policy/network binding, canonical genesis arithmetic, authority account balance and sequence, pending-slot admission, vote validation, certificate proof validation, and atomic in-memory settlement
boundary.mechanism: Validate a SignedTransfer, preflight sender existence/positive amount/sequence/balance before locking, then atomically apply a trusted certificate to authority balance and sequence together
non_goals: Durable authority recovery in this slice
Rolling interoperability with unsigned wire v1
Replacing the legacy local-credit Replica rail
boundary.state_authority: Each authority is the single writer for its local per-account balance, next sequence, and first-seen pending slot

state_model: A stateless owner/policy-authentication gate precedes a per-account FSM whose executable state is (balance, next sequence, pending order); confirmation changes balance and sequence in one authority-local commit or changes neither.

protocol.versioning: Signed order, vote, and certificate wire domains use v2, authority vote signatures use alias-bound domain v4, and unsigned v1 fails closed; mixed-cohort rolling upgrade is not promised.

invariants: No owner-authentication failure may create a vote, advance a sequence, mutate a ledger, or occupy a slot lock.
No unknown-sender, zero-amount, insufficient-balance, or out-of-order order may create a vote or occupy a pending slot.
Certificate settlement updates an authority's sender balance, recipient balance, and sender sequence together; execution failure consumes no sequence.
Duplicate genesis accounts, overflowing total supply, recipient balance overflow, and sequence overflow are rejected before any ledger mutation or authority vote.
The sender AccountId is bound to a verifier-owned Ed25519 key, never a caller-supplied key.
The sender, recipient, network id, sequence, and amount are all covered by the owner signature.
A certificate is valid only when its owner proof and a distinct authority quorum both validate for the same policy, committee, network, and transfer.
One authority public key may occupy exactly one committee identity, and the authority alias is covered by every vote signature.
Invalid votes are verified before collector deduplication and cannot poison a signer slot.

runtime.ordering: Owner/policy authentication is evaluated before pending-slot inspection; sender existence, positive amount, exact sequence, and sufficient balance are evaluated before a new lock.
runtime.concurrency: Different account slots may proceed independently; commands for one account are serialized by sequence and slot ownership.
runtime.backpressure: The authentication kernel owns no queue; the existing transport remains unbounded and must gain bounded ingress before production promotion.
runtime.cancellation: Certification collection is bounded by caller-supplied rounds; cancellation beyond process termination is outside this slice.
runtime.timeouts: TCP collection uses a bounded round count and pause; exhaustion emits a structured certification failure.

durability.persistence: None in this slice; authority locks and ledger state remain in memory and restart safety is not promised.
durability.atomic_commit: No durable commit exists in this slice; pending admission and certificate settlement are in-memory single-writer transitions, and a failed settlement does not advance sequence independently of balance.
durability.recovery: Process restart rebuilds only configured trust roots and genesis; WAL and snapshot recovery are the next engine slice.
durability.effect_idempotency: Owner and authority signatures are deterministic, votes are deduplicated after verification, and replayed old certificates return AlreadyApplied without a second debit or sequence increment.
durability.migration: All node processes must move to wire v2 as one cohort; unsigned v1 orders are rejected by domain mismatch.

failure_model: Wrong network, unknown sender, unknown recipient, and invalid owner signature are permanent rejections with no mutation.
Unknown authority-ledger sender, zero amount, and insufficient balance are permanent preflight rejections with no pending lock or vote.
Duplicate authority keys and invalid canonical genesis allocations fail during configuration before network startup.
Sequence or recipient-balance arithmetic overflow is a permanent preflight rejection with no pending lock, vote, debit, credit, or sequence advance.
Out-of-order and equivocation remain typed authority rejections after owner authentication.
Malformed or oversized length-prefixed wire fields and certificate vote counts are rejected before field allocation or state mutation.
Sub-quorum collection exhausts into an observable Certified::Failed outcome.

traces: Owner-auth rejection, state-preflight rejection, vote cast, certificate result, and ledger application carry a SHA-256 order identity without secret keys or signature bytes.
metrics: Owner-auth and state-preflight rejection counts, votes accepted, invalid votes dropped, quorum failures, and certificate applications.
observability.redaction: Secret seeds, private-key bytes, and full signatures are never emitted; public account ids and rejection classes are allowed.

security: Owner and authority signatures use separate domain tags.
PolicyId binds NetworkId and the sorted owner roster; CommitteeId additionally binds the sorted authority roster, and both are covered by the relevant signatures.
Committee construction rejects duplicate authority aliases and duplicate public keys; authority aliases are length-prefixed into the authority signature preimage.
NetworkId is an operator-assigned deployment/genesis/asset epoch name and must never be reused for a different genesis.
Committee configuration contains public keys only; secret-key loading is separate and explicit.
The test-only deterministic seed path is named dev-seed and is not a production credential format.
verification: A forged owner order arriving first gets zero votes and does not poison the valid owner's same slot.
A correctly signed overspend, zero amount, or registered-but-unfunded sender gets zero votes and does not consume the valid owner's same sequence.
Changing sender, recipient, sequence, amount, or network after signing invalidates the order.
A bad owner proof cannot become Verified even when authority signatures are otherwise valid, and a Verified value is branded by CommitteeId at application.
A vote signature copied from one authority alias to another is rejected, and a committee containing two aliases for one physical public key is unconstructible.
Duplicate genesis accounts and total-supply overflow fail construction; recipient-balance or sequence overflow returns a typed error before any ledger or pending-slot mutation.
Signed order, vote, and certificate v2 round-trip over the wire while unsigned v1 fails closed.
The real four-authority TCP harness rejects an impersonator before accepting the legitimate owner.
implementation_slices: OwnerRegistry, NetworkId, PolicyId, SignedTransfer, and owner-domain canonical bytes
CommitteeId-bound votes, authority auth/state-preflight-before-lock, and self-contained certificate validation
Authority-local balance/sequence settlement with typed no-advance failures
Alias-bound authority signature preimages, duplicate-key committee rejection, and checked genesis and settlement arithmetic
Public-key rosters plus separate authority and owner secret loading
falsifiers: Any unsigned network Order reaches Authority::handle.
A wrong-key Alice order produces one authority vote or prevents a later valid Alice order at the same sequence.
A signed overspend forms a certificate, occupies a pending slot, or advances authority sequence while its balance debit fails.
A certificate validates without independently validating the owner proof.
A vote or Verified value created for one policy or committee is accepted under another trust domain.
One physical Ed25519 authority key counts as multiple authority aliases toward quorum.
Any genesis, balance, or sequence arithmetic overflow panics, wraps, emits a vote, or partially mutates ledger or pending-slot state.
A committee roster value can be used to reconstruct an authority private key.
